title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection & Pinning - Aurora Financial
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results across candidate models, decide on version pinning strategy, and confirm rollback/fallback policies. SE demoed latency/cost tradeoffs, security questions raised about KMS and audit logs, and next steps include running q8 benchmarks and sharing a canary rollout plan.
next_steps: Redwood to run quantized (q8) benchmark with batch size 12 and provide p50/p95 numbers by 2026-10-25
Customer to provide 1 canonical eval set and 3 failure-case prompts by 2026-10-22
Schedule canary rollout planning session w/ Aurora infra on 2026-10-27
action_items: Miguel Santos (SE): run q8 + 16-batch benchmark on rtx-4k variant; deliver p50/p95 and token cost by 2026-10-25
Priya Kapoor (Customer): share canonical eval set and 3 hard failure prompts by 2026-10-22
Lena Park (AE): send updated pricing sheet and SSO/SAML notes by 2026-10-21
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 15:00 PT | Duration: ~50 minutes | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Aurora Head of AI), Ben Chu (Eng Mgr), Samir Patel (Security)

[00:00] Lena Park: okay everybody thanks for joining, quick check in — hope things are going well on your side?
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: yeah thanks Lena, been a busy week, um we ran the initial traffics through the three candidate models you suggested, wanted to talk results and then lock a pin strategy.
[00:18] Miguel Santos: great, thanks Priya. Quick recap — we ran baseline on redwood-hosted gaia-v1 and two open variants (gorb-13b and rdx-7b-q4) with your sample traffic. Some notes up front, transcription in the deck might say "Redwood Dedikated" in places — that's just our Dedicated offering, apologies for the typo in the slide deck.
[00:36] Ben Chu: ha no worries. On the results — can we go over p50/p95 latency and token cost?
[00:44] Miguel Santos: yes, p50 for gaia-v1 on hosted was about 190ms, p95 420ms, cost roughly $0.0018 per token (workload average). Gorb-13b gave p50 260ms, p95 640ms, cost a bit higher because of sequence length; rdx-7b-q4 was lowest cost but had some hallucination failures on the finance prompts.
[01:12] Priya Kapoor: that matches what we saw. The hallucinations were concerning on report-generation prompts — rdx produced invented ticker summaries.
[01:20] Miguel Santos: yeah that's expected with heavier quantization — tradeoff for cost. We suggested pinning strategy: pin gaia-v1 as primary for critical routes, fallback to rdx-7b for non-critical async jobs and to gorb-13b as an in-between for mid latency/cost.
[01:38] Samir Patel: quick security check — if we fallback between models, what happens to audit logs and key usage? We need end-to-end tracing that shows which model served the request and the key id used.
[01:50] Lena Park: good question. We persist per-request metadata: model_id, shard/host, and KMS key id for encryption actions. We can add explicit tagging for fallback reason in the logs so you can correlate. We'll share our doc for audit fields.
[02:05] Priya Kapoor: awesome, that's important. Also want to confirm SSO / SAML provisioning for Dedicated usage — we may move to Dedikated later but want to test hosted first.
[02:16] Lena Park: yes, SSO and RBAC are available in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we support enterprise SAML with SCIM provisioning for seats — Miguel will attach the SSO checklist.
[02:27] Miguel Santos: noted, I'll send the checklist and a short howto for mapping roles to route-level permissions.
[02:34] Ben Chu: back to pinning — what's the recommended version pin format? We want deterministic rollbacks.
[02:40] Miguel Santos: we recommend pinning at model-version level: e.g., gaia-v1@2026-10-12 and use a canary percentage rollout (5/20/100). If regression is detected, we can rollback the pin to a prior version. Also you can set fallback rules by policy — latency-first vs cost-first.
[02:58] Priya Kapoor: do you support automatic fallbacks on SLA breach? For example, p95 > 500ms then switch to backup model.
[03:05] Miguel Santos: yes, that's supported via routing policies — we can configure regional fallback and per-route latency thresholds. We'll propose a policy file in the canary doc.
[03:14] Samir Patel: about data residency — requests that hit fallback model might cross different infra, does that change where logs live? We need retention and residency controls.
[03:24] Lena Park: good catch. If you use Hosted and fallbacks to a different geography, we can restrict fallbacks to same-region variants only. For Dedicated/Private you get customer-controlled residency.
[03:36] Ben Chu: performance tuning question — Miguel you mentioned batching earlier. Our online inference is latency-sensitive, but some async jobs could handle batching. What knobs should we try?
[03:46] Miguel Santos: two main levers — batch size and cache TTL for KV cache/prefix caching. For online low-latency routes keep batching small (4-8) and aggressive cache warmups. For async backfills we can push batch to 16-32. Quantization (q4 vs q8) also saves memory and cost but can affect quality.
[04:05] Priya Kapoor: can you run a q8 benchmark? We saw q4 results that were too lossy.
[04:10] Miguel Santos: yes, we'll run q8 + batch 12 test on your workload. Expect numbers by Monday (2026-10-25). We'll include per-token cost estimates.
[04:19] Ben Chu: also include p10/p50/p95 and GPU utilization. If the utilization is spiky we might prefer Dedicated where we can reserve GPUs.
[04:26] Miguel Santos: will include util and a recommended Dedicated config if you want reserved pools.
[04:31] Priya Kapoor: any notes about model catalog naming — some of our engineers confused "gaia" and "gala" in the deck.
[04:37] Lena Park: oh that's on us, apologies — we had a slide typo. We'll resend a cleaned catalog.
[04:41] Priya Kapoor: thanks.
[04:43] Ben Chu: on the fallback behavior — if the primary returns a malformed JSON for structured outputs, will the fallback try the same system prompt? We need consistent prompts across variants.
[04:54] Miguel Santos: yes, prompt fidelity is preserved; fallback injects a small shim to adapt for tokenization differences but we keep system + user prompt identical. For structured output we attach a schema validator and can auto-fallback to a stricter model.
[05:08] Samir Patel: security again — KMS integration. Do you offer Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) in Hosted?
[05:13] Lena Park: Hosted supports customer-managed keys in certain tiers; Dedicated/Private support BYOK and HSM integrations. We'll include the KMS metainfo doc.
[05:22] Priya Kapoor: good. For rollout timing, our Q4 launch is tight. If we pin gaia-v1 now and later upgrade, what's the safest upgrade cadence?
[05:31] Miguel Santos: recommended cadence: test new version in staging for 2 weeks with full eval set, then canary 5% for 48 hours with auto-quality checks (BLEU/ROUGE/ task-specific metrics). If stable, ramp 20% for 24 hours then 100%. All this can be automated via our rollout hooks.
[05:49] Priya Kapoor: okay that sounds reasonable. Can we get the canary automation config example?
[05:54] Lena Park: yes we'll share a sample policy repo link in the follow-up.
[05:58] Ben Chu: anything else on pricing tradeoffs? We need guidance on when to move to Dedicated vs keep on Hosted.
[06:05] Miguel Santos: rule of thumb: when sustained throughput or predictability needs exceed hosted quotas, or when cost per token on hosted becomes more expensive due to high seq length, Dedicated becomes better. We'll model both for your expected Q4 traffic and show crossover point.
[06:18] Lena Park: action items recap — Miguel will run q8 benchmarks and send cleaned catalog; Priya to share eval set; Lena to send pricing and SSO notes. We'll also schedule canary planning session for 10/27.
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[06:35] Lena Park: thanks all — we'll follow up and post the benchmarks and docs. Meeting end.

References/Shared artifacts mentioned: "Aurora POC benchmarks.xlsx" (link shared in chat), canary policy sample repo (short link), SSO checklist PDF, KMS integration sheet.

Notes about transcription: occasional mislabels, some product names appear misspelled (Dedikated / gaia vs gala), filler words and overlaps preserved for realism.
